items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: at the CBS staff, you know, we had our Saturday afternoon show on the network with you on bass and Jo Jones on drums

ctx.x: Those little troops with Dizzy and Roy and starting out with Nat Cole and Oscar Peterson later and then Ella and Flip Phillips, Jo Jones, Gene Krupa
and Buddy Rich. Ray Brown. That carried the banner of jazz all over the world. They made a tremendous [impression], in Europe and Japan.

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: I'm pretty sure Brunswick. It was Billie Holiday recording date with Benny Goodman, Walter Page, Buck Clayton, Freddie Green , Mr. Teddy Wilson, and myself.

ctx.x: Can you remember anything that he might have played on a violin in the band?

If we did anything when we was at the Roseland for a month - if there was anything that he played that month, I would have to try to find some old dir shots that was made in 1936 coming into the first 2 weeks of January, because 'round about January the 17th or 18th we made a recording with Benny Goodman, Billie Holiday, Teddy Wilson,
